scope: scripts/qualify_graph_changes.py on a frozen Debug build of c8de3eb (D:\wp\b39), 38/38 steps, in one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with the authored native GRAPH seed FB (one step, one transition) imported through block_import_xml: graph_export returns the exact block software_inspect lists, retains the bytes of its native export (equal SHA-256) and leaves the project unchanged, refusing SCL and missing blocks; graph_edit renames step 1, and its result equals the source with every occurrence of the step name replaced (the step and its G7_StepPlus interface member) and nothing else, refusing a name an interface member uses (GraphEditDuplicate); graph_import applies the edited document with checkpoint, PLC compile and save, asserted preview and change_status, changing exactly the GRAPH block, whose native export carries the new name; a fresh owned Portal reopen shows the identical state and a second export, edit and import restored from its checkpoint equals the reopened state. Typed refusals (UnsupportedLanguage, BlockNotFound, XmlScopeMismatch, InvalidRequest, PreviewMismatch, StaleRevision) change nothing.
limitations: One GRAPH FB with one step and one transition; branches, jumps, actions, interlocks and supervisions are not edited natively.
graph_edit: renameStep only natively; the other typed operations are covered by the offline GRAPH tests.
Engineering only; no sequence is executed and behavioral equivalence is not certified.

steps: refuse graph_edit: a step name an interface member uses
refuse graph_import: a block outside expectedBlockNames
refuse graph_import: both graphRef and path
prepare import the renamed step (made stale below)
refuse apply graph_import: a wrong previewHash
refuse apply graph_import: a preview made stale by a later change
reopened state equals every verified change
prepare import the step renamed again
change_status import the step renamed again
snapshot import the step renamed again
verify import the step renamed again
restore import the step renamed again
snapshot restored import the step renamed again
restored import the step renamed again equals the pre-change state
